text.p: Australian biotechnology group ForBio Ltd said on Monday it intended to seek a secondary listing either on the London Stock Exchange or the pan-European Easdaq market, to raise funds for expansion.
ForBio said it had met institutions to complete a private placing to raise around $5.0 million but would be seeking around $20 to $25 million when it floats in Europe.
The group has developed a propagation robot which, combined with its gene mapping technology, can propagate disease-free plants in a soil-less, sterile environment.
ForBio already supplies seedlings to new forest plantations, for the production of potato minitubers and ornamental flowers, and is looking to expand into areas such as caffeine-free coffee beans.
The group said it was looking to develop its businesses through joint ventures.

Forbio, which is valued at about A$75 million (35 million stg) on the Australian Stock Exchange, made pre-tax operating profits of A$1.46 million in 1996, an increase of 89 per cent from the previous year.
Turnover jumped 245 per cent in 1996 to A$14.92 million.
